text:
Marco: Weird regression on sigma-int4 bring-up: vertical-subtitles test shows bracket/paren mirroring and Arabic phrase order flips when text contains mixed CJK + Arabic segments. chrF drops ~4.2 on the vertical-subset. Repro below.

Marco: repro:```bash
python -m evals.run --model sigma-int4 --suite vertical-subtitles-multilang --metric chrf --split smoke-500
```

Aya: Can you paste a minimal failing pair?

Marco: example (visualized line-by-line, original -> model):
```
REF: [	]  \u65e5
SYS:  [	]

REF:  (العَرَبِيَّة)
SYS: (العَرَبِيَّة) 
```
In short: brackets that should stay attached to following Arabic phrase end up swapped/mirrored; order inside parentheses is preserved but surrounding CJK punctuation jumps sides.

Rina: Is this happening only in vertical layout inputs or also horizontal?

Marco: only reproduces on vertical-subtitles suite (line-rotated layout). Horizontal test passes.

Diego: Could be bidi + layout transform bug where ZWJ/ZWNJ or directional embedding markers are dropped by tokenizer LUT compaction in int4. If directionality markers vanish, the renderer reflows brackets incorrectly.

Nina: Any differences between q8 and int4?

Marco: q8: tiny chrF delta ~0.4. int4: big spike. FP16 baseline clean.

EvalBot: failing_samples: 18; top_pattern: "mixed CJK + Arabic -> surrounding punctuation displaced"; attached artifacts: s3://evals/4855012345/vertical-artifacts.tar.gz

Aya: @Marco can you dump token id windows for one failing example in both fp16 and int4 runtimes? we need to see if directional control code points are present.

Marco: pasted token ids (decimal):
```
FP16: ... 305 412 8203 58 59 ...  // 8203 = ZWSP present
INT4: ... 305 412 0 58 59 ...   // becomes 0 in compressed table
```
ZWSP/embedding markers collapsed to zero index in quant LUT.

Diego: There's a recent change in quantizer remap logic that maps low-frequency control tokens to index 0 to reuse space. That was meant to be transparent, but apparently our tokenizer and renderer treat 0 as EOS/sep in the vertical layout path. Bad combo.

Rina: Quick repro idea: run tokenizer dump with `--show-control` flag to confirm presence on tokenization step vs runtime lookup. Also try `TOKENIZER_LEGACY=1` to force full table.

Marco: did a token dump: legacy mode retains 8203 and embedding markers; quant runtime map loses them. Legacy passes vertical suite.

Nina: So mitigation: exclude bidi/control codepoints from compression similar to the earlier kana issue? We should add ZWSP, ZWJ, ZWNJ, LRE, RLE, PDF, LRM, RLM to preserve list.

Diego: I'll open a quant-pipeline hotfix to reserve those code points. Patch ETA ~2h. Also propose a unit test that tokenizes mixed CJK+Arabic short-lines and asserts control codepoints not remapped.

Rina: Also add a smoke test to release regression suite for vertical layouts specifically. This one is easy to miss because horizontal passes.

EvalBot: job `quant-hotfix-preserve-bidi` started on build-host-7; notify: #eng-ml when complete.

Marco: Filed ticket ML-8799 with sample set, chrF diffs and stack traces. Linking artifacts in the ticket.

Aya: Nice catch. Once hotfix lands let's re-run canary on dedicated-int4 and if green promote. Also add a short note in bring-up checklist: "verify control-token preservation for vertical/bidi inputs".

(End of thread)
